The original NFT model is primarily concerned with representing a digital asset and establishing an on-chain ownership record.

That model solved an important problem.

It gave digital objects a persistent ownership layer that could be transferred and verified through blockchain infrastructure.

AINFT explores what happens when that concept is combined with artificial intelligence.

Instead of treating an NFT only as a static collectible, the asset can become associated with software, models, content generation, or agent-like behavior.

Ownership remains an important blockchain property.

The intelligent behavior can exist through software operating around that ownership layer.

That creates a distinction between the asset itself and the functionality connected to it.

The token can establish who owns the digital object.

AI infrastructure can determine what the object can generate, how it can respond, or what type of interaction it can support.

This creates a more dynamic interpretation of digital ownership.

An NFT does not necessarily have to remain frozen at the moment it is minted.

It can become a gateway into an application, identity, character, or intelligent digital experience.

For AINFT, that concept provides a direct bridge between the project's original NFT infrastructure and its current focus on AI.

The marketplace established a system for creating and circulating digital assets.

The AI layer explores how those assets can become more interactive.

That is one of the core ideas behind the project's broader transition from NFT infrastructure toward AI-native digital objects.

@AINFTcom @justinsuntron #TRONEcoStar

Today, G5 Labs is emerging from stealth with $14 million in seed funding to build a new abstraction layer for AI-native software development. @pillar_vc  and @BatteryVentures   co-led the round, with participation from @omegavp , Encoded Ventures, and prominent angel investors including @JeffDean . 

G5 Labs is pioneering the post-developer era. A spinout from MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL), the G5 Labs platform makes natural-language intent, organized as an ontology, the source code itself—putting software development in the hands of the whole organization while providing the governance needed to keep requirements, implementation, and organizational policies aligned.

We’re excited to build a future where employees across departments, from product owners to analysts and compliance leads, can create and evolve software using the language they already speak.

Stock News

Crypto bill blocked in Senate: Coinbase ($COIN)-backed advocacy group Stand With Crypto warned of electoral consequences after Senate Democrats blocked the Clarity Act, a key cryptocurrency regulation bill, ahead of the midterm elections. Source: Yahoo News.

AI leaders debate existential risks: Anthropic (private) CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing AI development to address risks, while experts highlighted concerns about AI's potential to threaten humanity. Source: The Guardian.

Global bond yields reach 2008 highs: Benchmark global bond yields surged to levels not seen since 2008, increasing borrowing costs for governments and corporations worldwide. Source: Yahoo Finance.

Federal Reserve set to hike rates: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its upcoming meeting, responding to persistent inflation pressures. Source: Fox Business.

Stocks fall as yields and oil rise: U.S. equities declined for a second day as the 10-year Treasury yield hit a 19-year high and crude oil prices topped $106 per barrel, ahead of the Fed decision. Source: CNBC.

U.S. income and poverty hit records: U.S. median household income reached an all-time high in 2025, while the official poverty rate fell to a record low of 10.2%, according to new Census data. Source: CNN.

Greg Brockman enters Forbes 400: OpenAI (private) president Greg Brockman debuted on the Forbes 400 list as the richest newcomer, with an estimated net worth of $25.5 billion. Source: Yahoo Finance.

Ford unveils 2027 F-150 refresh: Ford ($F) launched the 2027 F-150 pickup with hands-free towing, expanded V-8 engine options, and a new Carhartt edition, aiming to boost competitiveness in the truck market. Source: CNBC.

Nike co-founder donates $1.1B to healthcare: Nike ($NKE) co-founder Phil Knight and his wife pledged $1.1 billion to Providence St. Vincent Medical Center to build Oregon’s first dedicated women’s hospital. Source: CNBC.

Treasury defends Trump economic policy: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended President Trump’s economic record and recent Treasury interventions during a contentious House hearing ahead of the midterms. Source: CNBC.

AI giants discuss safety collaboration: OpenAI (private), Anthropic (private), and Google ($GOOGL) have held weeks of talks on industry-wide AI safety standards, as regulatory scrutiny intensifies. Source: CNBC.

September investing myth challenged: Financial advisors caution investors against overreacting to September’s reputation as a weak month for stocks, emphasizing long-term strategies over seasonal trends. Source: City Lifestyle.

Oracle announces layoffs and higher AI costs: Oracle ($ORCL) disclosed a new round of layoffs and said its AI transformation will cost an additional $700 million, as the company restructures to focus on cloud and AI services. Source: Business Insider.

Tesla Cybercab launch underwhelms: Tesla’s ($TSLA) highly anticipated Cybercab rollout failed to meet expectations, allowing Waymo (private) to solidify its lead in the U.S. robotaxi market. Source: Yahoo Finance.

Gates Foundation pledges $1B for AI equity: The Gates Foundation committed $1 billion to expand global access to artificial intelligence, warning that AI could exacerbate inequality if not managed responsibly. Source: ABC News.

Nvidia CEO calls for AI self-regulation: Nvidia ($NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang advocated for industry self-regulation on AI safety, while Anthropic’s CEO urged a more cautious approach, highlighting divergent views at a major tech summit. Source: CNBC.

Canada positioned as global finance safe haven: Former Bank of England Governor Mark Carney described Canada as a "safe harbour" for global finance, as Nova Scotia promoted clean energy investments at a national summit. Source: BBC.
